name: ESTA (Electronic System for Travel Authorization)

fee.text: US$40.62 per application. If you are refused, you pay only the US$10.62 processing part.

validity: 2 years from approval, or until your passport expires, whichever comes first, unless it is revoked.
applyAhead: Any time before you travel. CBP recommends applying as soon as you start planning, or before you buy your ticket.
maxStay: Visa Waiver Program visits of up to 90 days, for business or tourism.
officialOnly: Some websites charge a fee to submit your application for you. CBP can't refund money you paid to them.

legal_source.name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Official ESTA Application Website (FAQ)

name: UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)

fee.text: £20, online or in the UK ETA app. You can't get a refund after you apply.

validity: 2 years, or until your passport expires, whichever is sooner. You can travel to the UK as many times as you want while it is valid.
processing: Usually a decision by email within a day. It can take up to 3 working days.
applyAhead: Don't travel until you get the email confirming you have an ETA.
maxStay: Up to 6 months, for tourism, visiting family and friends, business or short-term study.
officialOnly: Other websites may charge more, and you can't get a faster decision through them. Avoid websites that imitate government services.

legal_source.name: GOV.UK, Get an electronic travel authorisation (ETA)

name: Korea Electronic Travel Authorization (K-ETA)
issuer: Republic of Korea Ministry of Justice

fee.text: KRW 10,000 per person (about US$7–8), plus an online payment fee of about 3%.

validity: 3 years, or until your passport expires if that is sooner.
processing: Usually 72 hours or less, but it can take longer. There is no expedited service.
applyAhead: You need approval before you board the flight or ship.
maxStay: K-ETA doesn't set your stay: the visa-free period for your nationality applies.
officialOnly: Korea hasn't delegated K-ETA applications to any agency. Apply only at www.k-eta.go.kr or in the K-ETA app.
notes: Temporary exemption: the passports that are currently exempt from K-ETA stay exempt until 31 December 2026 (Korean time). The K-ETA site doesn't publish that list as text; our South Korea entry page shows the rule for your passport.

legal_source.name: Korea Immigration Service, K-ETA official website

name: Australian Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601)
issuer: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs

fee.text: No visa application charge, but an AUD 20 service fee to use the Australian ETA app.

validity: 12 months, or until your passport expires if that is sooner. If you get a new passport, you need a new ETA.
processing: In most cases you get the result immediately.
applyAhead: Home Affairs suggests not making travel arrangements until your ETA is granted.
maxStay: Visit as often as you like in the 12 months, staying up to 3 months each time.

legal_source.name: Department of Home Affairs, Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601)

name: Australian eVisitor (subclass 651)
issuer: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs
validity: 12 months from the date it is granted.
applyAhead: Don't arrange your trip until Home Affairs tells you in writing that the visa is granted.
maxStay: Visit as often as you like in the 12 months, staying up to 3 months each time.

name: Kenya Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA)
issuer: Republic of Kenya, Directorate of Immigration Services

fee.text: From US$30 with normal processing (up to 72 hours). Expedited, immediate processing costs an extra US$100.

processing: Generally within 3 business days (72 hours), longer if verification takes time. Expedited applications are processed immediately.
applyAhead: Apply at least 2 weeks before you travel.
officialOnly: Apply only on the official website or the official "Kenya Travel Authorisation" app, with one application for each traveller.
notes: If you need an eTA, the application also asks you to buy Kenya's compulsory government travel health insurance.

legal_source.name: Republic of Kenya, eTA official website (FAQs)

_sources.name: Government of Kenya, eCitizen Inbound Travel Health Insurance

name: India e-Tourist Visa
issuer: Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs

fee.text: Depends on your nationality: see the official fee table. Banks add a 3% transaction charge, and the fee isn't refunded.

validity: Three kinds: 30 days (multiple entry, can't be extended or converted), 1 year or 5 years from the date it is granted.
applyAhead: Apply at least 4 days before your arrival date, and pay the fee at least 4 days before you travel.
maxStay: With the 1-year and 5-year visas, no more than 180 days in India in a calendar year.
officialOnly: The Government of India charges no emergency or express fee for an e-Visa.

name: Sri Lanka Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA)
issuer: Department of Immigration and Emigration, Sri Lanka

fee.text: Free since 25 May 2026 for tourists from 40 listed countries, for 30 days. Other nationalities pay the amounts on the official fee page.

validity: An ETA is valid for six months. You can't get a new one on the same passport until it expires.
applyAhead: Every foreign national needs one before arriving in Sri Lanka, including the 40 free-of-charge nationalities.
maxStay: 30 days, with a second entry allowed within those 30 days (90 days for Maldivian nationals).

name: Egypt e-Visa
issuer: Ministry of Interior, Arab Republic of Egypt

fee.text: US$30 single entry or US$65 multiple entry (tourism). The fee isn't refunded.

processing: No time is given: you get an email once it is processed.
applyAhead: Create your application at least 7 days before you leave.
